description: Shared test cases for the client-side extractors that turn a bash command line into the `command` values of an LLM usage record (go-llm-usage). Each client's extractor (Python, TypeScript) and go-llm-usage's own tests read this file, so they agree. `expected` lists one command per program run, in order, duplicates kept.
rules: Split the line into simple commands on unquoted `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, `&` and newlines, and on the case clause terminators `;;`, `;&` and `;;&`. `&` inside a redirection (`2>&1`, `&>`, `>&`) does not split.

Quotes group words and hide separators: what's inside quotes is never a separate command. That includes ANSI-C quotes (`$'...'`), in which a backslash escapes the next character. Command substitutions (`$(...)`, backticks) are not counted; quotes and backticks inside one hide its parentheses.

Shell data is never a command, whatever it holds. Skip: a comment (an unquoted `#` that starts a word, to the end of its line); a here-document's body (for each `<<WORD` or `<<-WORD` on a line, in order, the lines after it up to and including the one that is WORD -- with `<<-`, once leading tabs are removed -- quotes and backslashes in WORD removed; one never closed runs to the end); arithmetic, `(( ... ))` including `for (( ... ))`, and a `[[ ... ]]` test in command position, neither of which runs a program, so their `&&`, `||`, `|` and `;` do not split; and an array assignment's values (`NAME=(...)`, `NAME+=(...)`). A here-string (`<<< word`) is an ordinary argument.

A case statement's patterns are data. After `case WORD in`, a clause's pattern runs up to its unquoted `)` -- its alternatives (`a|b)`) and an optional leading `(` with it -- and its body is commands, up to `;;`, `;&` or `;;&`, after which comes the next pattern or `esac`. `esac` also ends a body. Case statements nest: one in a clause's body has its own patterns, and the outer clause resumes after its `esac`.

Unquoted `(` and `)` are words of their own even when attached to another (`(cd` is `(` then `cd`; `ci)` is `ci` then `)`). Drop leading `(`, `{`, `!` and the shell keywords `if`, `then`, `else`, `elif`, `while`, `until`, `do`. Drop simple commands that are only `)`, `}`, `fi`, `done`, `esac`, or that start with `for`, `case` or `function`.

Skip the wrappers `sudo`, `env`, `timeout`, `nohup`, `time`, `exec` and `command`, with every option (any word starting with `-`) that follows them. These options take a separate value, skipped with them: `sudo -u <user>`/`-g <group>`, `env -u <name>`, `timeout -s <signal>`/`-k <duration>`. Also skip `env`'s NAME=value pairs and `timeout`'s duration argument.
The program is the basename of the first remaining word (`/usr/bin/git` is `git`, `./test.sh` is `test.sh`). A program that doesn't match ^[a-z0-9._-]{1,32}$ is reported as `other`.

For a program in subcommand_programs, the subcommand is the first later word that doesn't start with `-`, skipping each listed value option together with its value (`git -C dir status` is `git status`). If that word doesn't match ^[a-z0-9._-]{1,32}$, or there is none, report the program alone.

cases.name: stacked wrappers
cases.command_line: sudo env FOO=1 timeout 10 /usr/local/bin/kubectl apply -f x.yaml

cases.name: semicolons
cases.command_line: mkdir -p out; cp a out/; ls out

cases.name: newlines
cases.command_line:
git add -A
git commit -m 'x'
git push

cases.name: subshell
cases.command_line: (cd web && npm ci) && npm run build

cases.name: if block
cases.command_line: if git diff --quiet; then echo clean; else echo dirty; fi

cases.name: for loop
cases.command_line: for f in *.go; do gofmt -l "$f"; done

cases.name: env wrapper with chain
cases.command_line: env GOOS=linux go build -o bin/x . && docker build -t x .

cases.name: ANSI-C quote with an escaped quote
comment
cases.command_line:
ls # a | secret2; rm x
pwd

cases.name: here-document body
cases.command_line:
cat > cfg <<EOF
password hunter2
rm -rf x
EOF
ls

cases.name: quoted here-document delimiter, with tabs stripped
cases.command_line:
cat <<-'END' | wc
	secret4
	END
git status

cases.name: two here-documents on one line
cases.command_line:
paste <<A <<B
secret5
A
secret6
B
ls

cases.name: indented delimiter does not close a plain here-document
here-document delimiter with a space
cases.command_line:
ls; cat <<"E O"
secret8
E O
wc

cases.name: case patterns
cases.command_line:
case $x in
  secret11) echo a;;
  secret12|other)
    make
    ;;
esac
ls

cases.name: a pipeline in a case clause
case on one line
cases.command_line: case $x in secret13) echo a;; esac

cases.name: case fall-through terminators
cases.command_line: case $x in a) ls;& secret15) pwd;;& secret16) id;; esac

cases.name: last case clause without ;;
cases.command_line:
case $x in
  a) ls
esac
pwd

cases.name: nested case
case inside if
cases.command_line: if true; then case $x in secret18) ls;; esac; fi

cases.name: subshell in a case clause
cases.command_line: case $x in a) (cd web && make);; esac

cases.name: arithmetic for loop
cases.command_line: for ((i = 0; secret21 < 3; i++)); do make; done

cases.name: test with a quoted bracket
cases.command_line: if [[ $x == "a ]] b" && secret23 ]]; then ls; fi

cases.name: single bracket test is a program
quoted parenthesis in a command substitution
parenthesis in backticks in a command substitution
